summary: The sole 94/81 occurrence is already the existing III Infectum example. Its longer weed-seed context adds background but no new verb form, sense, idiom or clearly better example cut; no duplicate is added.
komašrəʕ retains III sense 1 with livestock as subject and no overt emitted-object NP. u sarwo occurs in the following seed-mixture/result description, not as an object of this verb.

The local contrast with komabrəʕ and the edition's goats versus cattle/donkeys supports the inherited animal-dung distinction, but this single collective livestock clause does not independently prove a strict zoological boundary for each verb.
The denominative analysis and uncertain MEA slip etymology in the head remain as inherited. One agricultural-use context cannot establish the historical derivation.
Existing tēšriʕo is a grammar-page form citation; the supplied verse is finite Infectum and does not add a contextual Infinitiv attestation.

The edition translation prints tēṣrīʕo while the entry's Infinitiv is tēšriʕo and the running token komašrəʕ. Please verify the consonant/transcription difference against the edition; no source spelling is normalized.
How strictly does the mbrʕ/šrʕ contrast track animal type, and can the uncertain denominative/MEA etymology be resolved from evidence beyond this one occurrence?
